source_metadata.exact_title: B-cell depletion with obinutuzumab for the treatment of proliferative lupus nephritis: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial

extraction.strategy: single-pass whole-source extraction; source was 8 main-text pages plus 3 supplement pages and did not require semantic batching

findings: No duplicate atoms retained across main text and supplement.

Supplemental IgM/IgG results were retained as distinct safety-related quantitative results; B-cell depletion table data were not duplicated because main-text Figure 4 already covered those NOBILITY results.

extraction_limitations: Atoms represent independently reviewable assertions from the supplied article and supplement; cited studies were not re-extracted as primary-study evidence.
Week-104 efficacy analyses were exploratory and not multiplicity adjusted; this qualifier is preserved in tags/limitations rather than changing the reported result values.
Some figure-derived B-cell depletion percentages were read from the rendered figure because the PDF text layer did not fully expose the plotted labels.

The current LiteratureAtom schema has no dedicated fields for journal metadata, trial registration, study-level sponsorship, or a comparative risk estimate that is absent from the source; these are handled in report metadata/tags rather than fabricated.
schema_gaps: No study-level metadata container in LiteratureAtom itself.
No explicit field for endpoint multiplicity status or prespecified versus post hoc status; tags are used.
QuantitativeResult requires a single estimate even when a source reports only arm-level safety proportions; the obinutuzumab arm proportion is stored as estimate while both arm values remain in arms.
